title: Optional Signals, Unequal Burdens: A Narrow Duty to Supply Cover
status: argument proposal; no source investigation or independent critique performed
central_question: Can a co-maintainer of an optional disclosure practice owe low-cost cover for a legitimate confidential exception?

claim.text: A person who voluntarily accepts a governance role in a disclosure practice can owe a defeasible duty to prevent the practice from making a legitimate confidential exception readily identifiable; a truthful cover refusal is a fallback remedy when redesign is unavailable and cover is expected to reduce net risk.
claim.relation_to_selected_idea: NARROWED: preserves the participant-specific harmless-refusal proposal but limits special responsibility to accepted governance roles; mere membership is not sufficient.
scope_conditions: The confidentiality interest is independently legitimate.
The routine makes refusal informative despite formal optionality.
The agent accepted a role in setting, administering, or reinforcing the practice.
The proposed repair has low burden and is expected to reduce net privacy risk.
No stronger reporting, safety, expressive, or reliance obligation defeats the presumption.

premises.text: Formal permission to decline does not guarantee practical freedom when refusal exposes protected status.
premises.support: Conceptual distinction between rule-level optionality and information carried by observed behavior.

premises.text: A predictable compliance convention can make an exception's refusal diagnostic.
premises.support: Stipulated certificate example; deterministic inference under the stated convention.

premises.text: The target's individual opt-out does not remove the inference while the surrounding convention remains predictable.
premises.support: Same stipulated example; policy permission leaves the response pattern unchanged.

premises.text: A voluntarily accepted governance role can generate responsibility beyond equal capacity to assist.
premises.support: Undertaking, control of default, and expectation-maintenance; contrasted with an equally capable bystander.

premises.text: Where the co-maintainer can make a low-cost, truthful, effective repair and disclosure is not owed, fair terms can require repair.
premises.support: Burden-sharing within an accepted practice; subject to rights, duties, effectiveness, and displacement limits.

inference: P1-P3 show why formal opt-out permission alone can fail to protect confidentiality.
P4 supplies a role-specific reason for the practice's co-maintainer to act; without it, only a general easy-aid argument remains.
P5 identifies a bounded repair obligation and makes refusal only one possible fallback.
Therefore, some co-maintainers can owe a defeasible duty to repair the practice, potentially by harmless cover refusal.

worked_case.setup: Ten people; exactly one confidentially exempt person declines; nine non-exempt people ordinarily display a certificate.
worked_case.baseline: Under the stipulated convention, the single refusal identifies the exempt person.
worked_case.cover_model: If each non-exempt person independently declines with probability 1/3, an observed set of four refusers leaves each of those four equally likely to be the exempt person only under the simplified assumptions of a uniform prior, independent cover, and no side information.
worked_case.limit: The example demonstrates reduced certainty under a stipulated model, not adequate real-world privacy or empirical behavior.

objections.text: A duty to withhold truthful information uses participants' speech as a privacy device and can violate their autonomy; the target has no general veto over others' self-disclosure.
objections.response: Restrict the duty to accepted governance roles, give redesign priority, preserve stronger speech/reporting interests, and treat refusal as non-assertive only where the practice grants a genuine option.
objections.remaining_risk: The boundaries between non-disclosure, misleading implication, and protected expression need primary-source and case analysis.

objections.text: Bystanders with equal capacity and cost may owe exactly the same aid, so co-maintenance adds no special duty.
objections.response: Use a counterfactual that holds capacity, cost, knowledge, and benefit fixed while removing accepted governance responsibility.
objections.remaining_risk: The role-specific premise may fail; if it does, narrow to easy aid or reject the distinctive thesis.

objections.text: Cover may reduce certainty without producing adequate privacy, or may relocate suspicion to another person or data source.
objections.response: Require an explicit threat model and net-leakage assessment; prefer private collection, aggregate release, or other protocol redesign.
objections.remaining_risk: The model is illustrative and does not establish any real anonymity threshold.

failure_conditions: Mere membership cannot ground a distinct role duty.
The supposed confidentiality interest is unjustified.
Cover does not lower expected exposure or merely displaces it.
The burden is material or a stronger right, duty, or public interest overrides it.
The refusal operates as a false assertion or improperly controls another person's chosen self-disclosure.

novelty.reason: No external sources were retrieved or read; close work may exist on inferential/group privacy, role responsibility, fair procedures, or easy aid.
